experiment.title: Cross-language provider model-catalog normalization comparison
experiment.purpose: Compare the pinned Vultr Python and TypeScript catalog libraries against a shared, language-neutral set of model-catalog observations.
experiment.hypothesis: Both implementations normalize equivalent source observations into semantically equivalent catalog records while preserving exact pricing, modalities, capability metadata, diagnostics, and cache provenance.
controlled_variables: Identical source payload bytes for paired Python and TypeScript trials
Identical model identifiers and source observation timestamp
Pinned upstream source revisions recorded below
No provider credentials, inference calls, or runtime activation
acceptance_criteria: Paired implementations produce equivalent canonical records for shared valid fixtures.
Pricing values preserve exact source decimal strings and units.
Unknown fields and unsupported capability values remain observable.
Malformed-entry behavior is measured and recorded per implementation.
Cache freshness and fallback source are explicit in outputs.
Each result references immutable fixture, implementation, and source revisions.

versioning.major: Change to experiment design, response-variable definitions, or acceptance criteria.
